newsitem.title: USA: SAFECO to buy American States for $2.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: SAFECO to buy American States for $2.8 billion.

text.p: SAFECO Corp. said on Monday it agreed to buy American States Financial Corp. for about $2.8 billion, a deal that will make it the 12th-largest property casualty insurer in the United States.

The deal, which calls for SAFECO to pay about $47 a share, has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies. Lincoln National, which owns about 83.3 percent of American States' shares, has agreed to support the transaction.
Lincoln National said it will receive about $2.35 billion cash for its American States' stake and will be repaid $300 million in intercompany American States debt.
The sale of American States is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to be completed in three to four months, Lincoln National said.
Lincoln National said it will use about $2.15 billion of after-tax proceeds from the American States sale for acquisitions.
Lincoln National said its board of directors also has authorised it to buy back up to $500 million of its stock.

Lincoln National said an expanded stock repurchase programme and selective acquisitions in the life insurance, annuity and investment management businesses will enable it to manage any initial dilution from the loss of American States' earnings.
Lincoln National said it will focus on life insurance and annuity acquisitions with significant distribution capability.
In addition, the company said it will seek mutual funds acquisitions where it can broaden its product line, increase distribution and add economies of scale or improve the investment performance.
"When the sale of American States is completed, all of our businesses will be in alignment with our strategy," Lincoln National Chief Executive Ian Rolland said.

SAFECO said the new combined company would have had 1996 revenues of $5.9 billion. It added that it will enhance the product mix, geographic reach and network of independent agents of both operations.
Upon completion of the deal, the combined enterprise will nearly double the number of independent agents that currently work with either organisation, SAFECO said.

The acquisition will accelerate SAFECO's growth east of the Rocky Mountains and enhance its position in eight core Midwestern and Pacific Northwest states; Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Ohio, Michigan, Kansas, Washington and Oregon.

"The addition of American States to SAFECO will result in approximately 4,000 new agents, said Randy Stoddard, senior vice president of SAFECO Property/Casualty Insurance Companies, who will become president of the property and casualty operations on July 1.
"This is a key component of our growth strategy," he said.
In early trading, Safeco was up $1.31 at $43.94 on Nasdaq. American States was up $7.25 at $45.375 on the New York Stock Exchange. Lincoln National was up $2.875 at $65.75, also on the NYSE.
